## Summary

### Description

A short thallus with a stout midrib arises from a discoid holdfast, widening as it branches into flattened red-brown or red-purple fronds to a height of 20 cm. The fronds are thin and membranous, around 2.5 cm in width and may have a slight blue iridescence under water. Repeated branching gives it a bushy tangled appearance with the branches tapering to rounded tips. Morphology is variable and blades can be either erect or prostrate and broadly-wedged or strap-shaped. Margins may be smooth, undulating, denticulate or hooked. frequently with a blue iridescence underwater.

### Recorded distribution in Britain and Ireland

Distributed around Britain and Ireland, being recorded more commonly in the south and sparsely in the east.

### Global distribution

Found from southern Norway and the Faeroe Isles to Spain. Also recorded in the Mediterranean and Brazil.

### Habitat

Found subtidally growing on rock and Laminaria hyperborea stipes. Grows on shaded areas on the sides of deep pools or under the cover of Fucus species in the intertidal.

### Depth range

-

### Identifying features

  * Cryptopleura ramosa has numerous subdivided strap-like to broad, wedge-shaped blades.
  * Prostate blades are secured to the substratum by numerous haptera (a specialised, multicellular attachment structure).

# Cryptopleura ramosa (Hudson) Kylin ex Newton

Description: Thin, membranous, brownish red fronds, to 200 mm long. Frond ± dichotomously divided, becoming irregular in upper parts. Frond with spots of iridescence, with undulate, often proliferous margins, sometimes with flattened hooks or with rhizoidal attachment processes. Very variable in growth form and often mididentified. It is the commonest intertidal and shallow subtidal Delesseriaceae seaweed in the NE Atlantic.
Habitat: On rock, generally epiphytic, and Laminaria hyperborea stipes, lower intertidal and subtidal to 32 m, generally distributed, common.
Notes: Gonimophyllum buffhamii, a minute parasite, occurs rarely on subtidal plants of Cryptopleura on southern and western coasts.

# Polyneura latissima (Harvey) Kylin (BC)

This typically bright red species is highly variable in size, 1–30+ cm, and shape, being roughly obovate (Image A), to lobed (Image B) to highly dissected in exposed habitats (Image C). Regardless to the gross morphology, this species is easily (for most individuals) identified by its characteristic pattern of anastomosing veins, which are particularly evident in tetrasporangial individuals as the sori are produced in abundance between the veins (Image D). In some individuals the blades can become noticeably bullate between the venation (Image E). Tetrasporangial sori are round to oval, at times weakly elliptical (Image F) and the tetrasporangia have a tetrahedral division pattern (Image G). Mature females have cystocarps scattered across the upper 2/3 of the blade surface (Image H).

This species is widely distributed in BC, from low intertidal to deep subtidal (16 m) growing on rock and other hard substrata, including coralline algae, as well as occasionally on noncalcified algae. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
